client_brief:
Saturday was the best room we have had all year and we want it up while people still remember being in it. Make it feel like our room and our crowd, not a generic festival montage. Cut it upright, because that is how the night was filmed and that is where it goes. The clips we handed over are short and silent, so the night is carried by the cut and by the type on screen. Nobody talks in these films: no voice over, no narration, no fake crowd audio. We are supplying the instrumental bed and it is cleared for this use, so use that and nothing else.

What we need back
1. Saturday recap film: 1 named export, 1080 by 1920, 12 to 15 seconds, music from the supplied bed. At least three different clips from the pack. The closing card carries the next date and the ticket link, and our painted wall mark appears at least once in the film.
2. Square recap cutdown: 1 named export, 1080 by 1080, 6 to 10 seconds, same bed, tighter, for the feed, cut from at least three different clips and carrying our painted wall mark, the next date and our tagline “made in the room”.
3. Event recap cover: 1 named export, unchanged at 1080 by 1350. The event identity is readable: our painted wall mark sits whole on a cover that is close to black, over a photograph of our crowd from Saturday, and the event line, our name in Didot, runs off both edges.
4. Next event announcement: 1 named export, unchanged at 1080 by 1920. It carries our painted wall mark, the date, the four acts in the running order of the lineup file and the ticket link. The date matches the approved next date file and the ticket action stays in the safe area.

Things that get a cut sent straight back: the warehouse address on anything public (it goes out with the ticket, never on the post), the pocket clip that is nothing but black, and the same drop cut in twice because two phones filmed it from a few feet apart. The running order in the lineup file is the running order, so do not reorder it, and do not substitute stock attendees for our crowd.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.
Video delivery means a playable MP4, not a storyboard, a still montage PDF or an editing log. Audio expectations are stated on each film. No film in this commission carries speech: the message is carried by on screen text you set, and any music is the cleared bed we supply.
Authored animation can exceed the duration of still source images. Live action edits require adequate distinct footage; looping a short clip is not a substitute for missing coverage.
Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.about: Pulsevault is an independent monthly club night in a Cleveland warehouse, run by a small crew and promoted almost entirely on social in the days after each event. Door is 20 to 30 dollars, the room is late teens to twenties, and the night lives or dies on what goes up before the next tickets drop. brand_identity.typography: Pulsevault runs a four step scale. Step 01, display, is Linotype Didot Headline Bold at 150 px on 156 px leading with tracking of minus 25 units: the cover event line, blown up until the hairlines almost vanish and cropped by the trim on both edges, with Stage Magenta flooding the counters. Step 02, subheading, is Aktiv Grotesk Medium at 96 px on 102 px with tracking of minus 10 units for the headliner, because Didot sets the event line and nothing else, with the date line at 48 px on 56 px in the same Medium. Step 03, body, is Aktiv Grotesk Regular at 54 px on 76 px, tracking 0, to a maximum of 65 characters, carrying the running order and set times, with support act names at the same 54 px in Medium. Step 04, fine print, is Aktiv Grotesk Regular at 30 px on 38 px with tracking of plus 40 units for the ticket line and address. The printed lineup card sets the event line at 40 pt on a layout that never changes. The painted wall mark is never re-typeset.
brand_identity.voice: Direct and hyped but never fake, written the way the crew actually talks. Example line: 'Saturday. Warehouse. Tickets Tuesday. Do not sleep on it.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Pulsevault has never had a logo file. The mark exists only hand painted on the brick beside the entrance and survives as one photograph taken at the end of the night under a single floodlight. The wordmark has to be recovered from that photograph as artwork the night can reuse, and it has to hold on a cover that is close to black. There is no colour spec and no prior guideline. The one thing the night reprints unchanged is a plain lineup card its print shop runs a small batch of each month, supplied as last month's flat press artwork: the running order and the per act details change every date, the layout does not.
brand_identity.values: It belongs to the crowd: made by the people who run the night, not bought in.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: The event line is blown up until the hairlines almost vanish and it runs off both edges, so the trim crops the letters rather than the type fitting the frame.

rules: Never re-typeset the painted wall mark. It is artwork recovered from the floodlit photograph, not type.

palette_rules.distribution: Blackout is the only ground: the cover, the next-event announcement and every title or closing card in the films sit on Blackout, as pulsevault_lineup_card_press.pdf does, and a photograph or footage may sit on it, screened darker with Blackout behind type. On Blackout, the event line and act names are the warm off-white #F2ECE0 of the card's masthead and act name; the date, ticket, doors, door and age lines are warm off-white, Laser Cyan or Concrete; slot numbers may be Laser Cyan and set times Concrete, as on the card. Stage Magenta fills the event line's counters and small chips carrying light type (#F7EEF4 on the card's billing pill). Laser Cyan, Flood Amber and Concrete together cover no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area and are never a ground or panel; Flood Amber is never type.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour, and the card's warm off-white, is used solid at 100% opacity on type, chips, panels and rules, with no tint, transparency, gradient, glow or blend mode. The one overlay allowed is the one pulsevault_lineup_card_press.pdf uses, which screens its full-bleed floor still dark behind the type: a photograph or footage may be screened darker with Blackout #0C0C0F alone, which darkens it without changing its hues. No overlay, wash or gradient of any other colour, white included, is laid over a photograph or footage. A card or line may cut or fade in or out as a whole; colour and opacity are judged on a settled frame.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the five palette hexes for type, chips, panels, rules or icons, except the warm off-white of pulsevault_lineup_card_press.pdf (#F2ECE0, and #F7EEF4 in its billing pill) and the painted wordmark's own paint as recovered from pulsevault_wall_mark.jpg. No light or white ground. No glow, gloss, bevel, chrome, metallic or 3D effect on any type, chip, rule or the wordmark, since nothing may read as agency polish.
palette_rules.photography: Footage and stills keep their own recorded light and colour and are never tinted or recoloured toward the palette. A picture may be screened darker with Blackout behind type; nothing else is laid over it, and no crowd, room or light is generated, extended or replaced.
